basis: Written from each champion's abilities and the stored kit values, for the Pairing Explorer. General Draft Logic, not yet reviewed by alan: never a saved pairing, a score or a ranking.

notes.plan: Win the lane in short trades from range and take plates while staying hard to all-in.
why: Karma's Inner Flame and Ezreal's Mystic Shot both poke from range, so most trades end before the enemy can answer.
Karma's Inspire shield and speed turns an enemy all-in into a walk-away for Ezreal, who still has Arcane Shift.
strengths: Lane priority and plates without committing.
Hard to kill: two speed or escape tools plus a shield.
weaknesses: Neither starts a real fight: a lead has to be turned into objectives by the jungler or mid.
Karma's lane strength peaks early; a long, even lane favours most scaling bot lanes.
notes.curve: Karma is strongest before items, Ezreal through the mid game: the lane wants an early lead.

notes.plan: Nautilus wants committed engages; Ezreal wants to trade from range. The pair works when Ezreal follows the hook with damage rather than expecting to finish an all-in himself.
why: Dredge Line and Depth Charge give Ezreal a target that cannot dodge Mystic Shot or Essence Flux.
Ezreal adds damage from range but no crowd control, so Nautilus's root and knock-up are the whole lockdown.
strengths: Threat of a hook keeps the enemy lane from walking up to poke.
Point-click Depth Charge for dragon fights.
weaknesses: The kill often needs the jungler: Ezreal's damage alone rarely finishes a target Nautilus has locked.
If the hook misses, Ezreal is in a short-range fight he did not want.

notes.plan: Kill lane: Leona locks a target from level 2 and Draven's axes finish it.
why: Zenith Blade into Shield of Daybreak stuns long enough for Draven to land two or three Spinning Axes.
Draven's attacks detonate Leona's Sunlight on the target she marked, adding damage to every all-in.
strengths: Wins the first levels decisively and snowballs Draven's gold lead.
weaknesses: Both commit forward: once Leona has gone in there is no peel left for Draven.
Into strong disengage (Janna, Poppy) or a lane that can out-range the first engage, the plan stalls.
notes.curve: Both peak before items: a lead has to be converted while it lasts.

notes.plan: Kill lane: Nautilus's hook and auto-attack root give Draven a stationary target.
why: Staggering Blow roots on Nautilus's first attack, which keeps a target in place for Draven's axes.
Dredge Line can start a fight from range when the enemy stands behind minions less carefully.
strengths: Two layers of lockdown (hook, root, Depth Charge) for one target.
weaknesses: A missed hook leaves Nautilus far forward and Draven without his engage.
Little peel once Nautilus commits.
notes.curve: Both strong early; Draven's gold lead has to be converted.

notes.plan: Win short trades often and keep them winning: Milio keeps Lucian healthy and in range for the next trade, rather than starting fights.
why: Lucian's Vigilance adds damage to his next attacks when an ally shields or heals him, so every Milio shield adds damage to the trade.
Milio's Cozy Campfire extends Lucian's short attack range, and Breath of Life cleanses the crowd control that would end a Lucian dash.
strengths: Sustain lets the lane keep trading instead of backing.
weaknesses: No hard engage: Lucian's lead comes from trades, not from Milio starting kills.
Lucian falls off late; the lane's advantage has to become plates, dragons and tempo.
notes.curve: Lucian peaks before items; Milio keeps the lane alive long enough to use that window.

notes.plan: Skirmish around Kalista's lane pressure, with Renata turning fights and saving Kalista in them.
why: Renata's Bailout lets Kalista keep fighting through a lost trade, and Kalista's hops keep her alive long enough for it to matter.
Handshake roots or throws a target Kalista is already stacking Rend on; Fate's Call can throw Renata back into a fight or pull her out.
strengths: Strong dragon control: Rend executes objectives.
Hostile Takeover turns enemy engages around.
weaknesses: Kalista falls off late and needs her lane lead to become objectives.
Renata starts no reliable fight herself; Kalista's own Fate's Call is the duo's engage.
notes.curve: Strongest early and mid game; weaker once the enemy carries reach full items.

notes.plan: Protect the carry until her items: Braum stands beside Yunara and cancels the enemy's first move.
why: Every Yunara attack adds a stack of Braum's Concussive Blows, so her attack speed turns Braum's passive into a fast stun.
Unbreakable blocks the projectiles aimed at Yunara, and Glacial Fissure stops a dive on her.
strengths: Very good against hooks and projectile engage.
weaknesses: Engage that walks or dashes in (Leona, Alistar, Rell) gives Unbreakable nothing to block.
Weak early: the lane is played to reach items, not to win.
notes.curve: Both weak early; Yunara peaks late.

notes.plan: Protect to scale: Lulu makes Yunara very hard to kill until her items let her carry fights.
why: Whimsy turns a diver into a critter, and Wild Growth knocks up whoever is on Yunara and gives her the health to keep attacking.
Help, Pix! shields Yunara and adds damage to her attacks.
strengths: Very hard to dive: two separate tools stop an engage on Yunara.
weaknesses: Little lane pressure: an engage lane that wins level 2 sets the tempo.
Few ways to start a fight; the comp needs engage elsewhere.
notes.curve: Yunara is weak early and peaks late; Lulu keeps the lane even until then.

notes.plan: Fight on Rakan's engage: Rakan goes in, Xayah's feathers root everything he gathers.
why: Rakan's Battle Dance reaches Xayah from further away, so he can engage and dash straight back to her.
The Quickness and Grand Entrance knock up a group that Xayah then roots by recalling her feathers with Bladecaller.
strengths: Shared recall and the dash range are unique to this pair.
Featherstorm makes Xayah untargetable when the fight turns.
weaknesses: Rakan has to go in to start: a missed engage leaves Xayah with only Featherstorm to escape.
Both mid-game strong rather than early lane winners.

notes.plan: Caitlyn holds the lane alone with her range while Bard roams, then the two set up traps on targets Bard holds still.
why: Caitlyn's range lets her keep farming and pressuring while Bard collects chimes and roams.
Cosmic Binding stuns and Tempered Fate freezes a target, and Caitlyn places Yordle Snap Traps under it.
strengths: Map pressure: Bard's roams pull the enemy away from Caitlyn's lane.
Siege: Caitlyn's traps and range take towers.
weaknesses: Bard's roams leave Caitlyn two against one; she survives on range, not on peel.
Bard's ultimate can ruin a fight as easily as win it.
notes.curve: Caitlyn is strongest early and stays useful late; Bard grows through the game with chimes.

notes.plan: Range-bully lane: both poke, push and take plates from the first levels.
why: Inner Flame and Caitlyn's Piltover Peacemaker trade from range, and Karma's Focused Resolve root gives Caitlyn a target for a trap.
Inspire's speed lets Caitlyn chase a low target or walk away from an all-in.
strengths: Lane priority and the strongest early plate pressure of the saved Caitlyn pairs.
weaknesses: No hard engage: a lead has to be converted with the jungler.
Karma peaks early; into scaling lanes the advantage has to become plates and towers.
notes.curve: Both strong early; Caitlyn stays useful late, Karma fades.

notes.plan: Protect to scale with fast waveclear: Lulu keeps Sivir alive while her Ricochet clears waves and Sivir's team speed decides fights later.
why: Whimsy's speed and Wild Growth stack with Sivir's On The Hunt for engages or retreats.
Lulu's peel covers Sivir, whose only defensive tool is Spell Shield.
strengths: Waveclear and speed for the team: good for front-to-back fights and keeping vision.
weaknesses: Weak early lane: an engage lane can force fights before Sivir has items.
Neither starts fights; the comp needs engage elsewhere.
notes.curve: Sivir is weak early and peaks late.

notes.plan: Speed and tempo: Karma's lane pressure covers Sivir's weak early lane, and both give the team speed to engage or leave.
why: Karma's Mantra-empowered Inspire and Sivir's On The Hunt both speed up the whole team, which makes engages and retreats faster than the enemy's.
Karma's poke wins the early trades Sivir cannot win alone.
strengths: Tempo: rotations and objective setups happen faster.
weaknesses: Karma peaks early and Sivir late: the lane is strongest early, the fights later.
No hard engage in the duo.

notes.plan: Nautilus provides the reliable start Ziggs lacks; Ziggs turns locked targets and sieges into damage from long range.
why: Depth Charge and Dredge Line hold a target still for Bouncing Bomb and Hexplosive Minefield.
Ziggs's Satchel Charge and range take towers and plates once the lane has priority.
strengths: Siege and plates from range.
A start the carry cannot provide for himself.
weaknesses: Ziggs is immobile: once Nautilus has gone in, a diver reaching Ziggs has nobody to stop it.
A missed hook leaves the lane without its start.

notes.plan: Leona's stuns give Ziggs a stationary target; Ziggs adds damage and siege from long range.
why: Zenith Blade and Solar Flare hold targets inside Hexplosive Minefield and under Mega Inferno Bomb.
Ziggs's bombs detonate Leona's Sunlight from range.
strengths: Reliable engage and long-range follow-up.
weaknesses: Leona has little peel once she commits; Ziggs is immobile against divers.
Leona falls off late.

notes.plan: Long-range control lane: Ashe's slows set up Seraphine's roots, and both ultimates start fights from far away.
why: Ashe's attacks slow, and Beat Drop roots a target that is already slowed, so Seraphine's E turns every Ashe hit into a root.
Enchanted Crystal Arrow and Encore both start fights from long range, and Encore travels further through allies.
strengths: Picks and fight starts from range.
weaknesses: Neither can stop a committed dive for long; the comp needs frontline.
Both deal utility damage more than carry damage: mid or top has to supply real damage.

notes.plan: Alistar starts the fight and Jhin's long-range root and burst finish it.
why: Alistar's Headbutt and Pulverize combo lands a target Jhin's Deadly Flourish can then root, chaining two lockdowns.
Jhin's Curtain Call adds long-range damage after Alistar's engage.
strengths: Alistar's combo also peels divers off Jhin when used defensively.
weaknesses: Jhin's four-shot cadence and immobility make a lost fight dangerous for him.
Alistar can engage or peel, not both in one fight.

notes.plan: Leona's stuns hold targets still for Jhin's root and four-shot burst.
why: Zenith Blade and Solar Flare lock a target for Deadly Flourish and Curtain Call.
Jhin's high-damage shots detonate Leona's Sunlight.
strengths: Reliable engage for a carry who needs setup.
weaknesses: No peel left once Leona commits; Jhin is immobile.
Leona falls off late.

notes.plan: Alistar engages and peels; Ezreal adds damage from range and stays safe behind him.
why: Alistar's Headbutt-Pulverize combo either starts a fight or knocks a diver off Ezreal.
Ezreal's Mystic Shot and Essence Flux hit a target Alistar has locked without walking in.
strengths: Both engage and protection in one support.
weaknesses: Ezreal brings no crowd control, so an all-in leans on Alistar and the jungler to finish.
Alistar's combo is one cooldown: after an engage there is no peel left for a while.

notes.plan: Leona engages; Ezreal follows from range and detonates her Sunlight without walking in.
why: Ezreal's Mystic Shot detonates Leona's Sunlight from range, adding damage to every Leona engage.
Zenith Blade and Solar Flare give Ezreal a stationary target.
strengths: Reliable engage for a safe carry.
weaknesses: Ezreal brings no crowd control: the all-in still needs the jungler to finish.
Leona has no peel once she commits.

notes.plan: Dive together: Nautilus's crowd control marks the target and Kai'Sa follows onto it with Killer Instinct.
why: Every Nautilus immobilise adds Caustic Wounds stacks, and Killer Instinct lets Kai'Sa dash onto any target carrying her plasma.
Depth Charge and the auto-attack root give Kai'Sa time to finish the target.
strengths: Reach: the duo can hit a carry behind a frontline.
weaknesses: Both commit to the same target: if the dive fails there is no peel.
Kai'Sa wants items; an even early lane is fine, a lost one is not.

notes.plan: Yuumi attaches to Zeri and keeps her healthy and fast while Zeri farms toward her late-game damage.
why: Zeri's Spark Surge and Lightning Crash move Yuumi with her, and Yuumi's Zoomies heals and speeds her up.
You and Me! keeps Yuumi untargetable while attached.
strengths: Mobility and sustain late.
weaknesses: Very weak to hooks and walk-in engage in lane; Yuumi cannot stop an all-in.
Little lane pressure: the lane is played to reach items.
notes.curve: Both weak early; Zeri peaks late.

notes.plan: Trade and sustain: Nami's empowered attacks and heals keep Corki winning short trades until his items.
why: Tidecaller's Blessing empowers Corki's next attacks with a slow and bonus damage, and Ebb and Flow heals him while hitting the enemy.
Aqua Prison gives Corki a stationary target for Missile Barrage.
strengths: Sustain and poke in lane.
weaknesses: Nami's bubble is the duo's only start; a miss leaves the lane passive.
Corki is weak to hard engage early.

notes.plan: Alistar starts fights and peels; Corki adds burst and poke from range.
why: Alistar's combo starts a fight Corki can follow with Missile Barrage and Phosphorus Bomb.
When defended, the same combo knocks a diver off Corki.
strengths: Engage and protection in one support.
weaknesses: Corki's follow-up is from range; the all-in leans on Alistar and the jungler.
Alistar's combo is one cooldown.

notes.plan: Wombo lane: Neeko's Pop Blossom stuns a group and Miss Fortune's Bullet Time hits everyone stunned.
why: Pop Blossom and Tangle-Barbs hold several enemies still for the whole Bullet Time channel.
Neeko's disguise can hide the engage until it lands.
strengths: Area damage in grouped fights.
weaknesses: Both are immobile when caught; Bullet Time breaks if Miss Fortune is stopped.
Few tools against a hard dive on Miss Fortune.
